purpose: bounded source-recovery probe for the missing Asa Gray 146-genera close-species list

local_source.finding: The preserved HTML contains an editorial description of the 146-genera list, one literal Gray sentence, and AG signature. It does not contain the table/list rows or the lost covering note.

attempted_authoritative_sources.outcome: accessible through indexed search result; reproduces the same synopsis and two literal Gray blocks, identifies source as DAR 165:103, and provides no manuscript image or list rows
accessible through indexed search result as DAR 165 folio 92a:1r; this is Gray’s 30 June 1855 letter and the earlier close-species list, not the 1858 146-genera list at DAR 165:103
attempted_authoritative_sources.limits: It establishes an earlier 1855 list workflow and Gray’s bracket-marking practice only; it cannot supply the 1856-edition 146-genera rows or prove their later contents.

attempted_authoritative_sources.outcome: search result identifies manuscript catalogue and digital-image coverage in general, but the requested DAR 165:103 image/transcription was not retrieved in this probe

attempted_authoritative_sources.provider: Internet Archive scan surfaced via Wikimedia
attempted_authoritative_sources.outcome: printed correspondence compilation; search result contains Darwin’s related close-species discussion but no manuscript facsimile of Gray’s DAR 165:103 list
attempted_authoritative_sources.limits: A printed witness cannot recover missing handwritten rows or establish Gray’s original list extent.

attempted_authoritative_sources.provider: Cambridge University Library Darwin Archive overview
attempted_authoritative_sources.outcome: confirms DAR 159–184 are supplementary correspondence holdings, but provides no record-level DAR 165:103 facsimile in this probe

recovered_evidence.earlier_comparison: CUDL DAR 165 folio 92a:1r preserves Gray’s 30 June 1855 letter: he says he marks “close species” in unbound Manual sheets by brackets and sends them through Sir William Hooker. This is a distinct earlier list, not the 2249 list.
recovered_evidence.current_record: DCP-LETT-2249’s DCP page states the later list was taken from A. Gray 1856, while the first list was DAR 165:92/3 and the later source is DAR 165:103. The page also states the covering note is lost.
recovered_evidence.date_limit: Editorially, Darwin evidently received the list by 3 April 1858; Gray’s composition date remains undetermined. The XML broad lower bound 1809-01-01 is metadata scaffolding, not a composition date.

strict_limits: No 146-genera row, species name, count, handwriting, or Darwin annotation was recovered.
The 1855 CUDL witness cannot be substituted for the 1858 list.
No independent manuscript image was downloaded or preserved because none was located in the bounded public search.
The source remains partial: the surviving Gray sentence supports only the general qualification that most listed forms were distinct while some might not be; it does not reconstruct the table.
relationship_implication: The recovery probe does not alter existing review or evidence. It leaves DCP-LETT-2249 as a partial incoming list and does not establish additional source-complete links. In direction terms, Darwin 2252 is the reply to Gray 2249 for list receipt; this probe does not treat the edge as reverse.
